text: **[P-A] — Protocol-supported, ancillary.** The claim describes behaviour preserved in a transcript a third party can inspect, but which was not specified as an outcome in advance, had no control condition, and was recognized as relevant only retrospectively. The evidence is inspectable; the design is not. Stronger than [R], because the primary material can be read against our interpretation; weaker than [P], because nothing about the conditions was fixed before the fact. Where an ancillary observation functions as a near-control for a designed condition, this is stated in prose rather than given a further label.
